seo.title: Cruise Line Architect: Cruise Tycoon Game for iPhone & iPad
seo.description: Build a cruise line from one used ship and $75M. Design voyages between 204 real ports, fill every cabin and keep the fleet stocked. Free to play on iPhone.
seo.ogImageAlt: A white cruise ship under way at dusk, her decks glowing warm amber, with a dark coastline behind her and a golden sunset on the horizon
seo.keywords: cruise ship tycoon game, cruise line management game, cruise ship simulator, ship tycoon, cruise manager game

hero.imageAlt: A white cruise ship under way at dusk, her decks glowing warm amber, with a dark coastline behind her and a golden sunset on the horizon
hero.h1Sub: The cruise line tycoon game for iPhone and iPad
hero.lede: One second-hand ship, $75 million and every ocean on Earth. Design voyages between 204 real ports, put the right hull on each one, sell her cabins before she sails, and grow a single river boat or used ship into a fleet. You are the founder, never the captain.

intro.h2: A cruise line management game with real ports and real limits
paragraphs: Cruise Line Architect is a deep cruise-line management sim. Every port has a real berth length and channel depth, so the biggest ships don't fit everywhere and a river boat never leaves the river. Each departure has its own booking curve, and a ship that sails half-empty stays half-empty.

The money works the way the industry does: ticket revenue plus onboard spending, against fuel, crew, food, port taxes and travel-agent commission. Plan a long voyage badly and the fresh food runs out at sea.

highlights.body: The Caribbean, the Mediterranean, Alaska, the Danube, Northern Europe, New England, South America, Australia and the Pacific, the Far East, expedition-only Antarctica, and the 60-to-140-night world cruise. Each region has its own seasons.
highlights.alt: The world map zoomed on the Caribbean, with a ship on its route between Miami, Nassau, Cozumel and St. Thomas, and the speed controls above

highlights.h2: See the profit before she sails
highlights.body: Choose where guests board and where they leave, the ports of call, the nights and the fare. A live forecast answers every change with occupancy, revenue, costs and profit per sailing before you commit.
highlights.alt: The itinerary designer: nights and fare controls above a projected sailing with occupancy, revenue, costs and EBITDA per sailing

highlights.body: Draw the sea lane yourself. The course you draw sets the fuel bill, so a detour around a headland costs real money on every sailing.
highlights.alt: The route editor drawing the lane from Miami to Cozumel, with the distance, extra fuel cost and a clear-water check

highlights.h2: Stock her for the long haul
highlights.body: Plan where each ship loads fresh food, frozen and dry stores, and fuel. Buy at the pier or sign vendor contracts, and price every bunkering stop. An Antarctic expedition that runs out of fresh food costs you goodwill on every sailing.
highlights.alt: The supply plan for an Antarctic voyage, warning that fresh food runs out after 7 days, with the stores options and each stop's fuel and food

highlights.body: Order new from the yard, hunt the used market or charter. Hulls wear: send a tired ship for a drydock refresh or a full revitalization, and keep her five-year class survey current, or she can't sail.
highlights.alt: The fleet screen with a ship photo and a premium ship held in port out of class, her route on a small map and a note that she needs a drydock

details.h2: Run every part of the line

items.body: Tap any port for a short introduction, its berth and depth limits, and every route you run through it.
items.alt: The Nassau port card with a photo of the harbor, its region and a short introduction

items.body: Run world cruises of 60 to 140 nights, with open-jaw voyages that start and end in different ports.
items.alt: The Grand Pacific itinerary: a 100-night voyage from Fort Lauderdale across the Pacific and back, with its resupply status

items.body: Hurricanes, mechanical failures and port closures arrive as choices, and the clock waits while you decide.
items.alt: A hurricane warning in the Caribbean with two choices: reroute around it at a cost, or hold course and risk the line's reputation

world.h2: A cruise industry that moves around you

items.body: Cabins sell through the weeks before each departure, faster in the January-to-March wave season.
Twenty-three real rival lines redeploy their fleets by region and season and chase the same guests. Your reputation decides how hard they bite.
From a 190-guest Danube longship and an ice-class polar explorer to a 5,600-berth megaship.
Run launch campaigns and borrow against your fleet. With Pro, buy out a rival line or list your company once it's worth $500 million. Miss your payments and the lenders close in.

devices.body: Cruise Line Architect is built natively for iPhone and iPad. On iPad the map gets the whole screen beside a sidebar. Speed time up to 25× and watch the fleet cross the oceans.
devices.alt: Cruise Line Architect on iPad: the world map with ships on their routes beside the sidebar
bullets: Plays offline, with three save slots
Requires iOS or iPadOS 18 or later

pricing.h2: Free to play. Pay once to grow the fleet.
pricing.body: Cruise Line Architect is free to download. The free game gives you a fleet of up to two ships with every region, route design, resupply, vendor contracts, marketing, refits and borrowing. A single one-time purchase, Cruise Line Architect Pro, unlocks a third ship and beyond, buying out rival lines and taking your company public.
bullets: Restores on every device signed in to your Apple Account

faq.a: Yes. It's free to download and play with a fleet of up to two ships, with every region and system. A one-time purchase, Cruise Line Architect Pro, unlocks a third ship and beyond, buying out rival lines and going public. There's no subscription and there are no ads.
Yes. The game has 204 real ports in 11 cruising regions, each with a real berth length and channel depth, so not every ship fits every port.

faq.q: Can I design my own cruise itineraries?
faq.a: Yes. You choose where guests board and leave, the ports of call, the nights and the fare, and you draw the sea lane yourself. A live forecast shows the profit per sailing before you commit.

faq.q: What kinds of ships can I run?
faq.a: Six classes, from a 190-guest Danube river longship and an ice-class polar explorer to a 5,600-berth megaship. Order new from the yard, buy used or charter.

faq.q: Is Cruise Line Architect on Android or PC?
faq.a: Not at the moment. It's made for iPhone and iPad and requires iOS or iPadOS 18 or later.

faq.q: Do I need an internet connection?
faq.a: No. Your cruise line runs on your device. A connection is used for Game Center and the one-time purchase.

faq.q: Can I play the same game on iPhone and iPad?
faq.a: Saves stay on the device you play on, with three save slots. The Pro purchase restores on any iPhone or iPad signed in to the same Apple Account.

It's from the same studio and shares the business side: loans, going public and buying rivals. The cruise game adds its own systems: booking curves, berth and depth limits, open-jaw voyages, drawn sea lanes, resupply and class surveys.
